questions.q:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I : In H$_2$O$_2$, each oxygen atom is assigned an oxidation number of -1, In RbO$_2$, each oxygen atom is assigned an oxidation number of -$\dfrac{1}{2}$.
Statement II : Representation of HAuCl$_4$ and MnO$_2$ in stock notation is HAu(III)Cl$_4$ and Mn(II)O$_2$, respectively.
Examine the above statements and choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: H$_2$O$_2$ is a peroxide (O = -1) and RbO$_2$ is a superoxide (O = -1/2), so Statement I is correct. In HAuCl$_4$, Au is +3 (correct), but in MnO$_2$, Mn is +4, not +2, so Statement II is incorrect.

questions.q: a C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$ + b MnO$_4^-$ + c H$^+$ $\rightarrow$ x Mn$^{2+}$ + y H$_2$O + z CO$_2$. a and x respectively are
questions.explanation: Each C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$ loses 2 electrons and each MnO$_4^-$ gains 5 electrons; balancing electrons needs 5 oxalate and 2 permanganate ions, so a = 5 and x = 2.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Types of redox reactions): (a) Combination reaction (b) Decomposition reaction (c) Displacement reaction (d) Disproportionation reaction; List-II (Examples): (i) Cl$_2$(g) + 2Br$^-$(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2Cl$^-$(aq) + Br$_2$(l) (ii) 2H$_2$O$_2$(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2H$_2$O(l) + O$_2$(g) (iii) CH$_4$(g) + 2O$_2$(g) $\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ CO$_2$(g) + 2H$_2$O(l) (iv) 2H$_2$O(l) $\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ 2H$_2$(g) + O$_2$(g). Choose the correct answer.
options: a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - iv, b - iii, c - i, d - ii
a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
questions.explanation: Combustion of methane (iii) is a combination reaction, electrolysis of water (iv) is decomposition, the halogen displacement (i) is a displacement reaction, and disproportionation of H$_2$O$_2$ (ii) is a disproportionation reaction: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.q: In the reaction between hydrogen sulphide and acidified permanganate solution,
options: H$_2$S is oxidised to S, MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to Mn$^{2+}$
H$_2$S is reduced to S, MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to Mn$^{2+}$
H$_2$S is oxidised to SO$_2$, MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to MnO$_2$
H$_2$S is reduced to SO$_2$, MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to Mn$^{2+}$
questions.explanation: Sulphur in H$_2$S is oxidised from -2 to 0 (forming S), while Mn in MnO$_4^-$ is reduced from +7 to +2 (forming Mn$^{2+}$).

questions.q: In the titration of potassium permanganate (KMnO$_4$) against Ferrous ammonium sulphate (FAS) solution, dilute sulphuric acid but not nitric acid is used to maintain acidic medium, because
options: Nitric acid is a weak acid than sulphuric acid
It is difficult to identify the end point
Nitric acid doesn't act as an indicator
Nitric acid itself is an oxidising agent
questions.explanation: Nitric acid is itself an oxidising agent and would oxidise Fe$^{2+}$ independently of KMnO$_4$, interfering with the redox titration.

questions.q: In the reaction between moist SO$_2$ and acidified permanganate solution:
options: SO$_2$ is oxidised to SO$_4^{2-}$; MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to Mn$^{2+}$
SO$_2$ is reduced to S; MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to MnO$_4$
SO$_2$ is oxidised to SO$_3^{2-}$; MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to MnO$_2$
SO$_2$ is reduced to H$_2$S; MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to MnO$_4$
questions.explanation: 2MnO$_4^-$ + 5SO$_2$ + 2H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ 2Mn$^{2+}$ + 5SO$_4^{2-}$ + 4H$^+$: permanganate is reduced to Mn$^{2+}$ while SO$_2$ is oxidised to sulfate.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of S in H$_2$S$_2$O$_8$ ?
questions.explanation: H$_2$S$_2$O$_8$ (peroxydisulfuric acid) contains a peroxo (-O-O-) linkage, so two oxygen atoms are effectively at -1 instead of -2; accounting for this, the oxidation number of each S works out to +6, not the naive +7.

questions.q: aMnO$_4^-$ + bS$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ + H$_2$O $\longrightarrow$ xMnO$_2$ + ySO$_4^{2-}$ + zOH$^-$. a and y respectively are
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +4 (gain of 3e$^-$) and each S in S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ goes from +2 to +6 in SO$_4^{2-}$ (loss of 4e$^-$ per S, 8e$^-$ per S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$); balancing electrons, $3a=8b$ gives a=8, b=3, and since each S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ gives 2 SO$_4^{2-}$, y=2b=6.

questions.q: In which of the following compounds, an element exhibits two different oxidation states?
questions.explanation: In hydrazoic acid (HN$_3$, H-N=N$^+$=N$^-$) the three nitrogen atoms are not equivalent and carry different formal oxidation states, unlike the other compounds listed.

questions.q: Which of the following is not true for oxidation?
questions.explanation: Removal of an electronegative element is characteristic of reduction, not oxidation.

questions.q: The oxidation number of nitrogen atoms in NH$_4$NO$_3$ are
questions.explanation: In NH$_4^+$, N is -3 (each H is +1, ion charge +1); in NO$_3^-$, N is +5 (each O is -2, ion charge -1).

questions.q: In which of the following cases a chemical reaction is possible?
options: gold ornaments are washed with dil HCl
ZnSO$_{4(aq)}$ is placed in a copper vessel
AgNO$_3$ solution is stirred with a copper spoon
Conc. HNO$_3$ is stored in a platinum vessel
questions.explanation: Copper, being more reactive than silver, displaces Ag from AgNO$_3$ solution: Cu + 2AgNO$_3\to$Cu(NO$_3$)$_2$ + 2Ag; gold, platinum and copper-in-ZnSO$_4$ show no reaction.

questions.q: In the reaction of gold with aquaregia, oxidation state of Nitrogen changes from
questions.explanation: In aqua regia, HNO3 (N in +5 state) is reduced to NO (N in +2 state); the NO reacts further with Cl- to release nascent chlorine that dissolves gold.

questions.q: The number of moles of electron required to reduce 0.2 mole of Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ to Cr$^{3+}$
questions.explanation: Each Cr goes from +6 to +3 (gain of 3 e- per Cr, 6 e- per Cr2O7^2- ion since it has 2 Cr atoms); for 0.2 mol Cr2O7^2-, electrons required = 0.2 $\times$ 6 = 1.2 mol.

questions.q: For the redox reaction x MnO$_4^-$ + y H$_2$C$_2$O$_4$ + z H$^+$ $\to$ m Mn$^{2+}$ + n CO$_2$ + p H$_2$O, the values of x, y, m and n are
questions.explanation: The balanced ionic equation is 2MnO$_4^-$ + 5H$_2$C$_2$O$_4$ + 6H$^+$ $\to$ 2Mn$^{2+}$ + 10CO$_2$ + 8H$_2$O, giving x=2, y=5, m=2, n=10.

questions.q: 3ClO$^-_{(aq)}$ → ClO$^-$ + 2Cl$^-$ is an example of
questions.note: The equation as printed is likely a mis-transcription of 3ClO$^-\to$ClO$_3^-$+2Cl$^-$ (chlorine goes from +1 to +5 and to $-1$), which is a textbook disproportionation reaction, not a simple reduction; the KEA key nonetheless credits 'Reduction reaction', which is kept here as the official answer.
questions.explanation: The intended reaction is a disproportionation of ClO$^-$ (some Cl is oxidised to ClO$_3^-$, some reduced to Cl$^-$), but the KEA key marks this as a reduction reaction.

questions.q: H$_2$O$_2$ cannot oxidise
questions.explanation: Ozone (O$_3$) is a stronger oxidising agent than H$_2$O$_2$, so H$_2$O$_2$ cannot oxidise O$_3$; instead O$_3$ oxidises H$_2$O$_2$ to O$_2$ and H$_2$O.

questions.q: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.04 M K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ in acidic medium oxidizes a sample of H$_2$S gas to sulphur. Volume of 0.03 M KMnO$_4$ required to oxidize the same amount of H$_2$S gas to sulphur, in acidic medium is
questions.explanation: Equivalents of K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ (n-factor 6) = 50×0.04×6 = 12 meq; KMnO$_4$ (n-factor 5) needed: V×0.03×5 = 12, so V = 80 cm$^3$.

questions.q: In the reaction, 2FeSO$_4$ + H$_2$SO$_4$ + H$_2$O$_2$ $\rightarrow$ Fe$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ + 2H$_2$O, the oxidizing agent is
questions.explanation: Fe$^{2+}$ is oxidised to Fe$^{3+}$ while H$_2$O$_2$ is reduced to H$_2$O, so H$_2$O$_2$ is the oxidizing agent.

questions.q: The volume of 0.1 M oxalic acid that can be completely oxidized by 20 ml of 0.025 M KMnO$_4$ solution is
questions.explanation: Using $n_1M_1V_1=n_2M_2V_2$ with n(oxalic acid)=2, n(KMnO$_4$)=5: $2\times0.1\times V=5\times0.025\times20 \Rightarrow V=12.5$ ml.

questions.q: In chromite ore, the oxidation number of iron and chromium are respectively ...........
questions.explanation: Chromite is FeO.Cr$_2$O$_3$ (FeCr$_2$O$_4$), in which iron is +2 and chromium is +3.

questions.q: A white crystalline salt A reacts with dilute $HCl$ to liberate a suffocating gas B and also forms a yellow precipitate. The gas B turns potassium dichromate acidified with dilute $H_2SO_4$ to a green coloured solution C. A, B and C are respectively ...................
questions.explanation: Sodium thiosulfate with dilute HCl disproportionates to give sulfur (yellow precipitate) and SO$_2$ gas (suffocating), which reduces acidified orange K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ to green Cr$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$.
